To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CT of Cx50 could interact Ca2+-independently with the cytoplamic loop of Cx50 which mediate the binding of CaM with Cx50.
the CaM can bind to Cx50 through the interaction between the CT and CL of the Cx protein.
the CT could bind to CL Ca2+ independently and the CT-Cx50 interaction could mediate the CaM binding to Cx50 Ca2+ dependantly, which may be the important mechanisms for the Cx50 function in eye lens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intramolecular interactions of Cx50 and its binding with CaM.
the role of the intramolecular interaction and Ca2+-dependent CaM-binding to Cx50, and provides a novel mechanism of Cx50 in regulating gap junction channel activity.
the mechanism of the Ca2+-induced binding of CaM with gap junction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CT of Cx50 plays a critical role in mediating the CaM to the gap junction, which is important for maintenance of eye transparency.
the Ca2+-in-dependent intra- and inter- molecular interactions are critical in the function of Cx50.
the CT of Cx50 could interact Ca2+-independently with CL of Cx 50 and CaM could bind with CT Ca2+ dependenly, which may play a critical role in the regulation of gap junction channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+-independently interacting domain of CT of Cx50 is essential to mediate the CaM-dependent interaction between the Cx50 and the CaM.
the Ca2+-independently intramolecular interaction of CT and CL of the Cx protein is important for its biological significance.
the Ca2+-independently intramolecular interaction of Cx50 may mediate the CaM binding to Cx50, and the Ca2+ dependant binding of CaM may be involved in the regulation of Cx50 channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CT of Cx50 is critical for Ca2+-dependent localization of CaM, which may be involved in regulating the function of Cx50 in lens fiber cell.
the CT of Cx50 is important for the Ca2+-in-dependent interaction of Cx50 with CaM.
intramolecular interaction is critical in mediating Ca2+-dependent CaM binding to gap junction.
